source: NCERT Class XI, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch. 10 (Water in the Atmosphere).

sections.heading: 1. Humidity and Evaporation
points: **Water vapour** in the air = **humidity**; it comes from **evaporation** (and transpiration).
**Absolute humidity** = actual amount of water vapour (g/m³); **Relative humidity (%)** = ratio of actual to maximum vapour the air can hold at that temperature.
Warm air holds more moisture; when air is **saturated**, relative humidity = 100%; the **dew point** is the temperature at which saturation occurs.

sections.heading: 2. Condensation and Its Forms
points: **Condensation** = change of water vapour into liquid (when cooled below dew point).

sub: **Dew** — moisture on cold surfaces; **Frost** — dew below freezing.
**Fog and mist** — condensation near the ground (fog is denser); **smog** = fog + smoke.
**Clouds** — condensation at height around dust particles (condensation nuclei).

sections.heading: 3. Clouds
points: Clouds classified by height and form: **Cirrus** (high, wispy), **Cumulus** (heaped, cotton-like), **Stratus** (layered), **Nimbus** (rain clouds).
High clouds: cirrus, cirrostratus; middle: altostratus, altocumulus; low: stratus, stratocumulus, nimbostratus.

sections.heading: 4. Precipitation
points: **Precipitation** = water falling from clouds (rain, snow, sleet, hail).

sub: **Convectional** — heated air rises, cools (equatorial regions, afternoons).
**Orographic (relief)** — air forced up over mountains; windward side wet, leeward = **rain shadow**.

points: World distribution of rainfall is very uneven (heavy near equator/windward coasts, low in deserts/interiors).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Relative humidity (%) = actual vapour ÷ maximum at that temperature; dew point = saturation temp.
Condensation forms: dew, frost, fog, mist, clouds.
Cloud types: cirrus (high), cumulus (heaped), stratus (layered), nimbus (rain).
Leeward side of mountains = rain shadow (dry).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Relative humidity is a ratio (percentage)**; absolute humidity is an actual amount.
**Cirrus = high wispy clouds; cumulus = heaped; nimbus = rain-bearing.**
**Orographic rain** falls on the **windward** side; the **leeward** side is a **rain shadow**.
